title: Review: Rotational kinetic energy and rolling; Angular momentum and its conservation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: R05-ap1#t4 term and clue written for the game; R06-ap2#t3 term and clue written for the game; R05-ap1#t1 term and clue written for the game; R05-ap1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: R05-1#N.8b, R05-ap1#N.9, R06-1#N.3, R06-ap1#N.7, R06-ap2#N.9, R05-1#N.2, R06-1#N.6b, R06-ap1#N.10, R06-ap2#N.6, R06-1#N.11. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Slipping
items.clue: Condition in which a wheel's forward speed does not equal rω, so the surfaces slide.

items.label: Elliptical orbit
items.clue: Satellite path on which K and U trade while E and L stay constant; fastest when closest.

items.label: Work
items.clue: Torque times angle turned, for a constant torque; negative when the torque opposes the spin.

items.label: Kinetic friction
items.clue: Acts where surfaces slide over each other, dissipating energy and spinning up a skidding ball.

questions.stem: A thin-walled hollow ball (I = (2/3)MR²) is released from rest and rolls without slipping down a ramp. Its centre of mass descends a vertical height of 1.2 m. Use g = 10 m s⁻². What is the speed of its centre of mass at the bottom?

options.text: 4.9 m s⁻¹
3.8 m s⁻¹
4.0 m s⁻¹
3.5 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: A hoop is spun about its axle and then set down upright on a rough, level floor, with its centre at rest. At first the hoop skids, spinning in place; then it moves off and soon rolls without slipping. What happens to the hoop's total kinetic energy while it skids?

options.text: It stays the same: the rotational KE simply becomes translational KE.
It decreases: the rim slides on the floor, so friction dissipates energy.
It increases: friction pushes the hoop forward, doing positive work on it.
It stays the same: friction on a turning object does no work.

questions.explanation: While v_cm ≠ rω the contact point slides over the floor. Kinetic friction at a sliding contact turns kinetic energy into thermal energy until rolling begins.

questions.stem: A thin hoop (I = MR²) and a uniform solid disc (I = ½MR²) have the same mass M and the same radius R. The hoop rotates about its central axis at angular speed ω; the disc rotates about its central axis at 2ω. How do their angular momenta compare?

options.text: The hoop's is greater, since all of its mass is at the rim.
The disc's is greater, since it spins twice as fast.
They are equal: each is MR²ω.
The disc's is four times the hoop's, since L depends on ω².

questions.explanation: Hoop: MR² × ω. Disc: ½MR² × 2ω = MR²ω. Equal.

questions.stem: A student stands at rest at the edge of a turntable that is also at rest and can rotate with negligible friction about a fixed vertical axle. The student starts to walk counterclockwise around the edge, and the turntable starts to rotate clockwise. For which system is the total angular momentum about the axle constant while the student starts to walk?

options.text: The student and turntable together, as their torques on each other are internal
The turntable alone, since its axle exerts only negligible friction on it
The student alone, since she sets herself moving using her own muscles
No system, since friction acts between the student's feet and the turntable's surface

questions.stem: Car 1, of mass m, drives at constant speed v along a straight road that passes a lamp post at a perpendicular distance d. Car 2, of mass 2m, drives at constant speed v/2 along a straight road that passes the same post at a perpendicular distance 3d. What is the ratio L₂/L₁ of the magnitudes of the cars' angular momenta about the post?
questions.explanation: L = mv r⊥. Car 1: mvd. Car 2: 2m × (v/2) × 3d = 3mvd. Ratio 3, the same at every point of each road.

questions.stem: A uniform grinding wheel spins at constant angular velocity on a fixed axle, so its centre of mass stays at rest. A student claims: "The velocities of points on opposite sides of the wheel are equal in size and opposite in direction, so they cancel, and the wheel has no kinetic energy." Which response to the student's claim is correct?

options.text: It is right: the kinetic energies of points moving in opposite directions cancel.
It is right: a wheel whose centre of mass is at rest has no kinetic energy.
It is wrong: each moving point has positive kinetic energy, so the energies add.
It is wrong: the wheel's kinetic energy is (1/2)Mv², where v is its rim speed.

questions.stem: Counterclockwise is taken as positive. A motorized turntable with rotational inertia I is rotating counterclockwise with angular speed ω₀. The motor then brings it to rotate clockwise with angular speed 3ω₀. Using this sign convention for both the initial and final angular momenta, which expression gives the change in the turntable's angular momentum?

options.text: +2Iω₀
−4Iω₀
−3Iω₀
+4Iω₀

questions.stem: An astronaut floats inside a space station, touching nothing and holding nothing, and rotates slowly about an axis through her center of mass. Air resistance is negligible. Which of the following could change her angular momentum about that axis?

options.text: Pulling her arms and legs in close to her body
Twisting her torso one way and her legs the other
Pushing sideways on a handrail fixed to the station
Waiting, since spinning slowly dies away when nothing acts

questions.stem: A lump of clay moving horizontally in a straight line strikes and sticks to the outer edge of a door that is initially at rest. The door can rotate about vertical hinges with negligible friction. The collision decreases the kinetic energy of the clay–door system. Which statement about the angular momentum of the clay–door system about the hinge axis is correct?

options.text: It decreases, since the system's kinetic energy decreases.
It is the same just after the collision as it was just before.
It increases from zero, as the clay moved in a straight line.
It changes, because the hinges exert a force on the door.

questions.stem: A playground merry-go-round with a rotational inertia of 240 kg m² about its axis turns freely at 1.5 rad s⁻¹. A child of mass 40 kg, moving straight towards the axis, steps onto the edge, 1.5 m from the axis. Treat the child as a point mass. What is the new angular speed?

options.text: 1.2 rad s⁻¹
1.5 rad s⁻¹
1.3 rad s⁻¹
1.1 rad s⁻¹

questions.explanation: I after = 240 + 40 × 1.5² = 330 kg m². Iω constant: ω = 240 × 1.5 ÷ 330 = 1.1 rad s⁻¹.
